Implementation started (worktree off origin/main incl. blusterous d8fac898). Empirical exposure matrix on the build base (scratchy NOT yet landed):
- transition: force/reason/caused_by/ref exposed on library+CLI, NOT in MCP transition_ticket inputSchema (only close_class). close_class exposed on all three.
- claim: force exposed on library+CLI, NOT in MCP claim_ticket inputSchema.
So EVERY MCP divergence is a scratchy-leprous-galago gap -> all MCP param-gap rows get a strict-xfail citing scratchy; no untracked CLI gap exists (CLI parser accepts --caused-by behaviorally even though --help omits it).

Post-blusterous adjustment (as the plan anticipated): the transition coupled-force rows are NO LONGER strict-xfail-citing-blusterous -- blusterous landed, so lib+CLI agree; the only remaining divergence on those rows is the MCP gap (scratchy). No blusterous-citing xfail markers are introduced.

Mechanics: MCP non-exposure is detected precisely from the tool inputSchema.properties (the advertised client surface) -- that is exactly what gains the param when scratchy lands, flipping the strict-xfail to an xpass and forcing marker removal. CLI parity is proven behaviorally (the hand-rolled parser silently ignores unknown flags, so a silently-dropped param would surface as a blocked op under an enabled gate = a caught divergence). Reusing+extending tests/interfaces/adapters.py (Outcome + 3 adapters); adding tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py (the case table + executor) and tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py (the oracle).

compiled_state.description:
Build a behavioral CONFORMANCE ORACLE that mechanically asserts write-op parity across the lib, CLI, and MCP adapters, so surface drift is caught without an LLM, without a change-detector, and without a hand-maintained NxM matrix. It implements the behavioral-oracle design validated by a session prototype (design + empirical results recorded on ticket restoring-shallow-blobfish; the prototype script is a throwaway session artifact, NOT a committed repo file, so this ticket builds the durable suite from scratch rather than promoting a checked-in file).

## Context / Problem
The write ops (transition/claim/create) are exposed through three adapters — the Python lib, the CLI, and the MCP server — but their input surfaces are hand-mirrored. A param present on one can silently be missing on another (exactly the MCP gaps captured in sibling scratchy-leprous-galago: reason/caused_by/ref/force). Nothing mechanically guards against this drift today; it is caught only by chance or by LLM review.

## Approach
Build a durable pytest CONFORMANCE ORACLE (Pattern B, proven in OSS: Python DB-API / SQLAlchemy dialect compliance, the CommonMark spec suite, WSGI/ASGI validators). ONE transport-agnostic contract table holds rows of (op, inputs, expected accept | reject-with-rule, expected effect). Each row is executed through every adapter against a fresh temp store and classified ACCEPTED / REJECTED(rule) / PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED; any divergence between adapters on the same row fails the suite. This asserts BEHAVIOR — including the runtime conditional-required rules (close_class required iff bug-close; reason required for REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) — which shape/signature generation cannot express. We deliberately do NOT generate the surfaces (Pattern A): behavior is already single-sourced through composer.create_core / transition_compute / claim_compute, and the adapters carry irreducible hand-written value (MCP LLM-facing docstrings, CLI ergonomics), so regenerating them would risk agent/user-visible contract breaks.

The contract covers the SANCTIONED surface: `force` (str | None — the reason-carrying `--force[=<reason>]` param, matching `claim`), `reason` (str, close_reason role only), `caused_by`, `ref`, `close_class`. `force_close` is intentionally EXCLUDED from the contract — it is a redundant param being removed by sibling blusterous-earthly-kitten; the oracle tests the consolidated `--force[=<reason>]` bypass (force carries its own audit reason), not the legacy param.

Cross-ticket sequencing (declared, not undeclared): the reason-carrying `--force[=<reason>]` / `force: str | None` shape ALREADY exists on `claim` today, but on `transition` it is INTRODUCED by blusterous-earthly-kitten (today transition's lib force is a bool + separate reason + force_close). The oracle therefore encodes the transition coupled-force rows as strict-xfail citing blusterous-earthly-kitten — exactly the same mechanism as the MCP gaps below — so the suite is GREEN in CI before blusterous lands and the rows xpass (forcing their un-xfail) once it does. This keeps the oracle independently landable in either order rather than hard-blocking on blusterous. Known current MCP gaps (reason/caused_by/force not exposed on transition_ticket/claim_ticket) are likewise encoded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago, so the suite is GREEN in CI today and closing a gap makes the strict xfail fail (xpass) — the intended forcing function for cleanup. Because both scratchy (MCP) and blusterous (transition force) are in flight, the un-xfail of their rows is expected on convergence and is the signal to delete the corresponding xfail markers in the same or a fast-follow change; the oracle does not depend on either landing first.

## Scope
- tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py — new conformance suite.
- tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py — new shared contract table (the single source of cases).
- REUSE and EXTEND the existing three-adapter harness tests/interfaces/adapters.py (already imported across the interfaces tier): it provides `Outcome`, the `Adapter` protocol, and `LibraryAdapter` / `CliAdapter` / `McpAdapter` with a shared ACCEPTED/REJECTED rejection-identity mapping — exactly the substrate the oracle needs. The existing `transition(tid, current, target)` / `claim(tid, assignee=None)` signatures do NOT yet thread the write-op inputs under test, so extend the `Adapter` protocol and its three implementations to pass `force`, `reason`, `close_class`, `caused_by`, `ref` through each transport. Do NOT build fresh parallel drivers or reuse the ad-hoc _FakeMCP/_FakeCtx capture; the interfaces sandbox-repo bootstrap (tests/interfaces/conftest.py) already backs adapters.py.
- Cover the transition, claim, and create write ops across all three adapters via the extended adapters.py drivers.
- Treat source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root as adapter-bound internals (NOT contract params) so they do not register as false divergences.
- No CI-provider-specific trigger: runs as an ordinary pytest (portability).

## Testing
- Run `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`: green in CI, with the current MCP reason/caused_by/force gaps recorded as strict-xfail rows referencing scratchy-leprous-galago.
- Include one reason-required bug-close row and one close_class-missing row to assert the runtime conditional rules behaviorally on every adapter (both REJECTED consistently across adapters).
- Include a negative-control row over an adapter-bound internal (e.g. source) to confirm it is NOT flagged as a divergence.
- A committed, re-runnable in-suite check (a simulated-parity fixture, not a one-time manual step) flips a strict-xfail row to xpass, proving the oracle detects convergence and would then require the marker's removal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single shared contract table drives all three adapter drivers; adding a new op is one new row (verified by inspecting the module: one table, three drivers).
- [ ] The contract covers `force`(str, the `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying param)+`reason`+`caused_by`+`ref`+`close_class` and does NOT include the legacy `force_close` param (grep the table).
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py` passes in CI, with the current MCP reason/caused_by/force gaps captured as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago (visible in the test output).
- [ ] Runtime rules (close_class-required, reason-required) are asserted behaviorally for every adapter (the two rows exist and reject consistently).
- [ ] Adapter-bound internals (source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root) produce no false divergence (negative-control row passes).
- [ ] The suite reuses and extends the existing tests/interfaces/adapters.py three-adapter harness (Outcome + Adapter protocol + Library/Cli/Mcp adapters), threading force/reason/close_class/caused_by/ref through it — no fresh parallel drivers (verified by inspecting imports).
- [ ] The transition coupled-`--force[=<reason>]` rows are strict-xfail citing blusterous-earthly-kitten (introduced there, not present on transition today), keeping the suite green in CI regardless of landing order (visible in test output).
- [ ] A committed, re-runnable simulated-parity check flips a strict-xfail row to xpass in-suite (not merely recorded as a ticket note), proving the oracle detects the fix.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green.
